title: Daily routine
goal: Describe your daily routine and habits, say how often you do things, and say what you're doing right now.
intro:
This is the unit where Nepali verbs really come alive. You'll learn the **present habitual** — म गर्छु 'I do', ऊ जान्छ 'he goes' — with all its endings for person, gender and respect, and its negative (गर्दिनँ 'I don't do').

You'll also learn the **present continuous** for what's happening right now: म खाँदै छु / म खाइरहेको छु 'I'm eating'.

vocab.en: to put on, wear; to apply

vocab.note: Irregular past: गयो 'went'. म जान्छु, तपाईं जानुहुन्छ.

vocab.en: to sleep; to go to bed; to lie down

vocab.note: The great helper verb: नोकरी गर्नु, फोन गर्नु, सफा गर्नु…

vocab.en: to walk; to leave, set off

vocab.note: म कहिल्यै ढिलो उठ्दिनँ 'I never get up late'.
Links clauses/events in speech; र links nouns.
ढिलो भयो 'it's got late / I'm late'.

phrases.en: What do you do every day?
I always have tea in the morning.

phrases.native: म दस बजेदेखि पाँच बजेसम्म काम गर्छु।
phrases.roman: ma das bajedekhi pāṃch bajesamma kām garchhu.
phrases.en: I work from ten to five.
In the evening I cook dinner.
I go to bed at eleven at night.
On Saturdays I do the laundry.
Sometimes I walk to the office.
Hurry up, we're late! (to a friend)

grammar.title: The present habitual: म गर्छु 'I do'
grammar.body:
Take the dictionary form, remove **-नु** to get the stem, and add the endings. For consonant stems (गर्नु → **गर्-**):

म **गर्छु** *garchhu* · हामी **गर्छौँ** *garchhauṃ*
तँ **गर्छस्** *garchhas* · तिमी **गर्छौ** *garchhau*
ऊ **गर्छ** *garchha* · उनी/उनीहरू **गर्छन्** *garchhan*
तपाईं/उहाँ **गर्नुहुन्छ** *garnuhunchha* (the -नु form + हुन्छ)

For **vowel stems** add -न्छ-: खानु → **खान्छु, खान्छ, खान्छन्**; जानु → जान्छु; धुनु → धुन्छु. Stems in -आउ/-उ- get a nasal: आउनु → **आउँछु**, पकाउनु → पकाउँछु.

**Women**: in careful Nepali the 3rd person has feminine forms: ऊ **गर्छे**, उनी **गर्छिन्** (and तिमी गर्छ्यौ). Kathmandu speech often uses the masculine forms for everyone, but you'll hear and read both.

The present habitual is used for **habits, general facts and the near future**: म भोलि जान्छु 'I'll go tomorrow'.

examples.en: What time do you go to sleep?
Mother goes to the temple in the morning.

grammar.title: The negative habitual: गर्दिनँ, गर्दैन
grammar.body:
The negative uses **-द-** + negative endings (vowel stems: **-ँद-**):

म **गर्दिनँ** *gardinaṃ* · हामी **गर्दैनौँ** *gardainauṃ*
तँ **गर्दैनस्** · तिमी **गर्दैनौ** *gardainau*
ऊ **गर्दैन** *gardaina* · उनी/उनीहरू **गर्दैनन्** *gardainan*
तपाईं/उहाँ **गर्नुहुन्न** *garnuhunna*

Vowel stems: खानु → **खाँदिनँ, खाँदैन**; जानु → **जाँदिनँ, जाँदैन**; आउनु → **आउँदिनँ, आउँदैन**.

You already know some of these as fixed phrases: **पर्दैन** 'no need', **हुँदैन** 'it won't do / not allowed', **थाहा छैन** 'I don't know' (that one uses छैन).

grammar.title: What's happening now: गर्दै छु / गरिरहेको छु
grammar.body:
Two ways to say 'I am doing':

**1. stem + -दै + छ**: म **गर्दै छु** 'I'm doing'. Vowel stems take -ँदै: खाँदै छु, आउँदै छु. Often written as one word: गर्दैछु.
**2. stem + -इरहेको + छ**: म **गरिरहेको छु** — slightly more emphatic 'I'm in the middle of doing'. Vowel stems: खाइरहेको, आइरहेको.

Only the छ part conjugates: तिमी गर्दै **छौ**, उनीहरू गर्दै **छन्**, तपाईं गर्दै **हुनुहुन्छ** (or गरिरहनुभएको छ). Negative: गर्दै छैन / गरिरहेको छैन.

dialogue.title: Early bird
dialogue.setting: Pemba and Sarah, colleagues at an NGO office, chat over morning tea.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: सारा, तपाईं बिहान कति बजे उठ्नुहुन्छ?
lines.roman: Sārā, tapāiṃ bihāna kati baje uṭhnuhunchha?
lines.en: Sarah, what time do you get up in the morning?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: म सधैँ छ बजे उठ्छु, अनि योग गर्छु।
lines.roman: ma sadhaiṃ chha baje uṭhchhu, ani yog garchhu.
lines.en: I always get up at six, and then I do yoga.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: वाह! म त आठ बजेभन्दा पहिले कहिल्यै उठ्दिनँ।
lines.roman: wāh! ma ta āṭh bajebhandā pahile kahilyai uṭhdinaṃ.
lines.en: Wow! I never get up before eight.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: And how do you get to the office?

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: प्रायः माइक्रोमा आउँछु। कहिलेकाहीँ हिँडेर पनि आउँछु।
lines.roman: prāya māikromā āuṃchhu. kahilekāhiṃ hiṃḍera pani āuṃchhu.
lines.en: Usually by microbus. Sometimes I walk, too.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: What do you do in the evenings?

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: घर गएर खाना पकाउँछु, अनि समाचार हेर्छु। तपाईं नि?
lines.roman: ghar gaera khānā pakāuṃchhu, ani samāchār herchhu. tapāiṃ ni?
lines.en: I go home, cook, and watch the news. And you?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: म बेलुका नेपाली पढ्छु। अहिले पनि नयाँ शब्दहरू पढ्दै छु!
lines.roman: ma belukā nepāli paḍhchhu. ahile pani nayāṃ sabdaharu paḍhdai chhu!
lines.en: I study Nepali in the evenings. I'm reading new words right now too!

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: त्यसैले तपाईंको नेपाली यति राम्रो छ!
lines.roman: tyasaile tapāiṃko nepāli yati rāmro chha!
lines.en: That's why your Nepali is so good!

culture: A typical Nepali day starts early: tea at dawn, a visit to the temple or a walk, then the first big meal of **dal bhat around 9–10 a.m.** before school or work. Offices usually open at 10 and close at 5; **खाजा** (snacks, tea) fills the afternoon, and the second dal bhat comes around 7–8 p.m. Saturday is for laundry, family visits and, for many, a lie-in. In cities, people commute in crowded **माइक्रो** (microbuses), **टेम्पो** and on motorbikes.
